transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (BlueCrest Head of Security), Maria Chen (BlueCrest CTO), Evan Park (BlueCrest SRE Lead)
Links shared: security-whitepaper.pdf (link), SOC2_attestation_2025.pdf (link), hsm-integration-diagram.png (to be shared)

Summary: Quick security review focused on encryption at rest/in transit, KMS options, BYOK and HSM integration, key rotation and access controls. BlueCrest has strict FIPS/HSM requirements for payment data and needs clarity on Redwood's BYOK model, HSM connector options and audit log granularity.

Topics: encryption at rest, envelope encryption, KMS vs BYOK, external HSMs, key rotation, audit logs, SSO/RBAC touches, data residency, TLS/FIPS requirements

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining um we'll give a quick run through on our encryption model and then priya will dig into the BYOK HSM questions, uh happy to take questions as we go
[00:22] Tom: thanks alex, quick note, we have the legal folks on standby but main asks are HSM-backed keys and if you can meet FIPS 140-2/3 certifications, and how audit logs look for key usage
[00:45] Priya: yeah totally, so at a high level redwood supports encryption in transit with TLS 1.2/1.3 and all data at rest is encrypted by default; we use envelope encryption so customer data keys are wrapped by a root key managed in our KMS
[01:08] Maria: when you say "our KMS" do you mean redwood's managed KMS or we can bring our own? we have policy to use our own HSM in some regions
[01:25] Priya: both — we offer managed KMS which is our default (backed by cloud KMS in region), and we support BYOK where customers provide keys; for strict HSM requirements we offer an HSM connector pattern and also support cloud HSM options like AWS CloudHSM if you want dedicated hardware
[01:50] Evan: is the HSM connector one of those on-prem bridges or is it a service you host? what's the flow?
[02:05] Priya: good q — two patterns: 1) customer-managed KMS in their cloud (eg AWS KMS or Google KMS) where redwood calls the customer's KMS over a secure VPC peering or private link; 2) BYOK with an HSM that sits on-prem or in a customer VPC where we call via a mutually authenticated mTLS channel using a connector agent. we'll share the diagram after this call
[02:35] Tom: and in the second pattern, does key material ever leave the HSM? we need absolute assurance it never exported
[02:48] Priya: no, for the HSM-backed flow keys are never exported; we use the HSM to perform wrap/unwrap operations and envelope encryption so the plaintext data key doesn't leave the HSM. the wrapped key is stored in our metadata but wrapped under customer's root key
[03:15] Alex: to add, we also support HSM-backed cloud KMS like AWS CloudHSM where the customer controls the HSM and policies and we call it via AWS KMS APIs; so you can pick whichever fits your compliance controls
[03:35] Maria: what's the latency impact? we run low-latency inference in prod, a synchronous KMS call per request could add ms to tail latency
[03:50] Priya: great point — we do prefix/KV caching for the runtime keys; the typical flow is: generate a data key, cache the unwrapped data key in a secure in-memory cache (with TTL) on the serving node, and only call KMS on key rotation or cache miss. so per-token inference doesn't hit KMS on every token
[04:22] Evan: how long is that cache TTL and is it configurable? we need limits to meet our data governance
[04:35] Priya: default TTL is 1 hour but it's configurable per workload. we surface policy controls in the console and via API to set TTL, rotation cadence, and eviction behaviour
[04:50] Tom: audit logs — we need cryptographic proof of key usage and an immutable trail. what does redwood provide?
[05:05] Priya: we log key usage events with timestamps, request IDs, calling principal and region; logs are delivered to the customer's audit sink if you're on Dedicated or Private, or we provide filtered exports for hosted customers. logs include KMS call traces, wrap/unwrap operations, and admin actions. we can also push to your splunk/siem over syslog or to cloud storage
[05:40] Maria: for hosted customers, how long are logs retained and can we request longer retention?
[05:55] Alex: hosted by default 90 days for detailed logs, with aggregated metrics retained longer. for enterprise customers we offer extended retention as an add-on or via Dedicated/Private where you control retention policies
[06:18] Tom: do you have a signed attestation for SOC 2 and pen test results we can share with risk?
[06:30] Alex: yes i'll send SOC 2 attestation and the latest pen test summary after the call, link included in next steps
[06:42] Evan: okay about key rotation — do you support automated rotation and can we force rotation from our KMS?
[06:55] Priya: yes, rotation can be automated by policy, and in BYOK / external KMS models you can trigger rotation from your side and we will pick up the new wrapped key on next fetch. we document the rotation handshake in the integration guide
[07:18] Maria: one of our regs wants FIPS 140-2 validated crypto in the data path — does redwood run on FIPS modules or support FIPS-compliant builds?
[07:35] Priya: our crypto stack uses FIPS-compliant algorithms; for FIPS-validated modules we recommend Dedicated/Private deployments where we can run validated libraries and ensure underlying OS/Crypto modules meet FIPS requirements. we'll need to map exact control numbers with your compliance team
[07:58] Tom: how do you manage RBAC and who can trigger key unwraps inside your org? we need strict separation of duties and least privilege
[08:12] Priya: we have role-based access controls integrated with SSO (SAML/SCIM), and administrative actions are gated by RBAC and MFA. key management actions (create/delete/rotate) are limited to a small set of service principals and require approval workflows in Dedicated/Private; for hosted customers we provide logs and an audit trail
[08:38] Evan: do you surface a view of which service principal called KMS for each request in the logs?
[08:46] Priya: yes logs include calling principal and request ID. we also sign the log downloads for tamper evidence on Dedicated/Private
[09:00] Alex: quick note on network — we support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and customer-managed NAT, and we prefer private connectivity for KMS calls to avoid public endpoints
[09:20] Maria: data residency: our payment data must remain in EU region, can you guarantee that?
[09:32] Priya: yes, with region pinning you can lock model serving and storage to a region; with Dedicated/Private we can ensure the control plane is in your VPC or on-prem, and keys never leave region when using local KMS options
[09:50] Tom: about BYOK onboarding, what does the key provisioning flow look like practically? is there an API or do we upload key material?
[10:05] Priya: we have an API where you can register a key by providing the wrapped key material (never plaintext) or connect to your cloud KMS via IAM role. for HSMs we provide an integration guide and a connector that performs a handshake to register the key; we do not accept plaintext keys over the wire
[10:30] Evan: is the connector agent open source or managed?
[10:36] Priya: it's a lightweight agent we supply (binary) that runs in your VPC; we can open-source parts of it but currently it's distributed under an enterprise license, can be air-gapped or run as a managed connector depending on your needs
[10:55] Maria: curious about key compromise scenario — if a key is compromised how do you revoke and rewrap historical data?
[11:08] Priya: we support key rotation and rewrap operations — you can retire a key and re-encrypt data with a new key. for large datasets we have background rewrap jobs, and for live inference we rotate with minimal disruption by keeping backward compatibility for a short window while rewrap completes
[11:35] Tom: and can we require dual control or multi-person approval for key deletion?
[11:44] Priya: yes for Dedicated/Private deployments we can configure dual control workflows; hosted customers can request elevated controls but it's easier with Dedicated. we'll document the exact approval steps
[11:58] Alex: one more on HSM: we support both PKCS#11 and cloud KMS APIs; for on-prem HSMs we use a connector that communicates over mTLS and performs PKCS#11 operations in the HSM
[12:20] Evan: ok what's the expected outage impact if KMS is unreachable — do you have graceful degradation?
[12:31] Priya: yes, we've got fallback policies: cached keys continue to serve for TTL, and we can fail open for reads or fail closed for writes based on policy. for PII-sensitive workloads you probably want fail-closed but we can configure per-route fallback policies
[12:58] Maria: for incident response, can we get a signed timeline of key events?
[13:08] Priya: we can produce signed audit exports and provide forensics packages for enterprise customers; these include key usage, admin actions, and correlated request traces
[13:28] Tom: do you integrate with our SIEM (we use Splunk + SQS) for real-time alerts?
[13:40] Priya: yes we can stream logs to Splunk, to a cloud storage bucket, or push to an SQS/SNS endpoint for alerting. we also support webhooks for admin events
[13:58] Alex: quick check — any blocker on compliance side so far?
[14:04] Tom: main open questions: proof of HSM non-export, FIPS module mapping, extended log retention, dual control for deletion, and exact BYOK onboarding steps. plus latency/mode impacts for inference
[14:22] Priya: we'll follow up with an HSM integration diagram and a doc that maps our controls to your compliance controls; we'll also propose a small benchmark plan to measure latency with the HSM flow
[14:40] Maria: would like the benchmark to include cold-start latency and key rotation scenario, and some tail p95 numbers for our production profile
[14:55] Priya: noted, we'll include p50/p95 and heavy-load burst test and a step that simulates KMS unavailability to test fallbacks
[15:12] Evan: one more on encryption algorithms — do you support AES-GCM and AES-KW for wrapping?
[15:22] Priya: yes we support AES-GCM for data encryption and AES-KW or RSA-OAEP for wrapping depending on KMS capabilities; specifics are in the integration guide
[15:40] Alex: i want to call out that for customers on Dedicated we can ship an HSM appliance integration and do co-managed setups if needed
[15:55] Tom: any change in how you do key custody if we go to Dedicated vs hosted?
[16:05] Priya: Dedicated gives you more control — customer-managed KMS endpoints, private connectivity, and the ability to keep logs and key metadata in your environment; hosted uses redwood's managed infrastructure but can still support BYOK via connectors
[16:28] Maria: regarding encryption at rest for backups and snapshots, are those also wrapped under the same KMS keys?
[16:40] Priya: yes backups and snapshots are encrypted with the same envelope workflow and wrapped under the customer's root key when BYOK is used; snapshots can be restricted to region and have separate retention policies
[16:58] Tom: what about multi-tenant isolation — how do you ensure keys from customer A aren't used or leaked to B?
[17:10] Priya: keys are namespace-scoped and metadata includes tenant id; the runtime enforces tenant isolation at the process level and we have access controls and audits to prevent cross-tenant access. tenant separation is stricter on Dedicated/Private where entire pools can be dedicated
[17:34] Evan: wanted to check certificate management — do you support centralized cert management or do we upload certs to the connector?
[17:45] Priya: we support both — we rotate mutual TLS certs via our cert management service or you can upload certs to the connector and manage yourself; cert rotation can be automated via ACME or triggered manually
[18:03] Maria: on legal side, if we need a DPA addendum for key custody language can you accomodate that?
[18:12] Alex: yes we have addenda for BYOK and HSM clauses and can work with legal to add the specific custody language
[18:25] Tom: any third party attestations for HSM vendors you work with?
[18:33] Priya: we list supported HSM vendors in the docs and provide mappings; for cloud HSMs the vendors have their own attestations and we rely on that, for on-prem we can discuss vendor-specific validation steps
[18:50] Evan: timing for pilot — if we want to run a pilot, what's the minimal setup?
[18:58] Priya: minimal pilot: a Dedicated trial or a Private single-tenant instance with a connector to your test HSM; we'll do onboarding, a short benchmark run, and a compliance checklist. estimate 2-4 weeks depending on provisioning
[19:20] Maria: budget check — is HSM connector part of enterprise plan or add-on?
[19:29] Alex: connector support and extended retention are enterprise add-ons; exact pricing we'll send after this call
[19:40] Tom: ok let's recap and assign actions
[19:46] Priya: recap: we'll share the HSM integration diagram, the BYOK onboarding steps, and a proposed benchmark plan. alex will send SOC2 and whitepaper. bluecrest will confirm policy and residency constraints
[20:03] Alex: i'll put links in the follow-up email and cc priya and evan, also include the legal addendum template
[20:12] Maria: thanks, we may need a deeper technical session to walk through PKCS#11 logs and the connector code path
[20:22] Priya: happy to run that — we can do a 90-min technical deep dive with our infra team next week
[20:33] Evan: fine. we'll aim for the week of 2026-03-22, tentative
[20:38] Tom: thanks everyone
[20:42] Alex: thanks all, talk soon

End summary & explicit next steps: Alex to send SOC2 attestation and encryption whitepaper (done by 2026-03-17). Priya to share HSM integration diagram and BYOK flow and integration guide (by 2026-03-20). Schedule technical deep dive (90m) week of 2026-03-22 to validate connector and run key rotation tests.
